intro: Three kinds of unease survive in the painted figure.
alt: Three differently painted portraits with uncanny stillness, playful distorted marks and a scraped interior.

variants.name: Magic Realism
variants.look: The crisp face and suspended steam feel strangely deliberate.
variants.history: Franz Roh coined the term in 1925 for a strand of European painting that found mystery in precise everyday scenes.
variants.when: Make an ordinary room unsettling through lighting, scale and stillness.
variants.why: Precisely observed surfaces make a single improbable detail stand out.

variants.name: CoBrA
variants.look: Thick bursts of red and blue and playful outlines warp the portrait.
variants.history: CoBrA took its name from Copenhagen, Brussels and Amsterdam and embraced experimental, spontaneous image-making.
variants.when: Let paint and gesture loosen an otherwise formal pose.
variants.why: Uneven contours and thick strokes hold the energy of spontaneous invention.

variants.name: School of London
variants.look: Worked and scraped paint presses the figure into an intimate interior.
variants.history: R. B. Kitaj gave the name to a loose grouping of London-based, figurative painters in 1976.
variants.when: Let the material build-up register the time spent looking at a sitter.
variants.why: Layers and erasures make prolonged observation physically visible.

prompt: Draw a single textless art comparison board for a museum-quality online art atlas. Layout is three equally wide vertical rectangular triptych cells, edge-to-edge, no gutters or borders; precise, strictly equally sized cells. Order is left to right within each row, then next row. Each cell is a distinct style treatment featuring the same female executive from reference, in original new art. The reference image is for identity only: recognizable ash-blonde hair in neat low bun with four-color windowpane hair clip, black-rimmed rectangular glasses over blue eyes, charcoal sheath dress under fitted black blazer, azure pocket square and blue lanyard with blank ID badge, holding a white coffee mug with a little four-color tile mark. Change the actual render style rather than adding only backgrounds. Layout styles in order: Magic Realism: eerily crisp, muted figurative office, anatomically precise, uncannily long shadows and a perfectly suspended steam curl; CoBrA: unruly childlike black contours, thick scarlet and cobalt paint, playful asymmetrical face and animal-like signs; School of London: heavy fleshy impasto, brush-scraped face and dark sienna seated figure held in a cramped room. No readable text, numbers, signatures, words, or extra panels.
